name: Exxon Mobil
legalName: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (Texas; successor registrant to Exxon Mobil Corporation, New Jersey, since July 1, 2026)
description: ExxonMobil is the largest US-listed integrated oil and gas company. It finds and produces crude oil and natural gas (4.7 million oil-equivalent barrels a day in 2025, with growth in the Permian Basin, Guyana and LNG), refines crude into fuels, makes petrochemicals, and sells specialty products such as lubricants. Most of its profit comes from Upstream (21.4 billion dollars of 2025 segment earnings out of 32.4 billion), yet most of its revenue comes from buying and selling fuels: Energy Products is about three quarters of external revenue at thin margins. Earnings swing with oil and gas prices and refining margins; in Q2 2026 earnings were 14.5 billion dollars against 7.1 billion a year earlier as Middle East supply disruptions and refining capacity cuts lifted prices and margins. It paid a dividend of 4.00 dollars per share in 2025 and plans 20 billion dollars of buybacks in 2026. Corporate and Financing costs and the emerging Low Carbon Solutions business (carbon capture, hydrogen, lithium) sit outside the four operating segments.

businessLines.name: Upstream
businessLines.shareBasis: 39,389 of 323,820 million total segment external sales and other operating revenue
businessLines.how: Sells crude oil, gas and LNG at market prices, mostly to its own refineries, to traders and to utilities under long-term LNG contracts; earnings move with commodity prices and volumes produced.
businessLines.description: Exploration and production of crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids worldwide (Permian Basin, Guyana, LNG in Qatar, Papua New Guinea and others).

revenue.note: External sales and other operating revenue (U.S. 25,396 + non-U.S. 13,993); a further 62,406 million is intersegment sales, mostly to ExxonMobil's own refineries.

businessLines.revenueNote: External sales and other operating revenue (U.S. 25,396 + non-U.S. 13,993); a further 62,406 million is intersegment sales, mostly to ExxonMobil's own refineries.

operatingProfit.note: Segment earnings after income tax (ExxonMobil share); 2024: 25,390

businessLines.name: Energy Products
businessLines.how: Buys crude and sells refined fuels; earns the refining margin (product price minus crude and running costs) on very large volumes, so revenue is huge but profit is a thin and volatile spread.
businessLines.description: Refining crude oil into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other fuels and selling them through wholesale, retail-brand (Exxon, Mobil) and trading channels worldwide.

revenue.note: External sales and other operating revenue (U.S. 99,073 + non-U.S. 145,378); the segment also pays 22,445 million of other taxes and duties on fuel

businessLines.revenueNote: External sales and other operating revenue (U.S. 99,073 + non-U.S. 145,378); the segment also pays 22,445 million of other taxes and duties on fuel

businessLines.name: Chemical Products
businessLines.how: Sells commodity plastics and chemicals to manufacturers at market prices; profit is the spread over feedstock cost and is currently squeezed (Q2 2026 margins below the bottom of the 10-year range).
businessLines.description: Petrochemicals: olefins, polyolefins, aromatics and intermediates for packaging, consumer and industrial goods; plants in the US, Singapore, China and elsewhere.

revenue.note: External sales and other operating revenue (7,594 + 14,615)

businessLines.revenueNote: External sales and other operating revenue (7,594 + 14,615)

businessLines.name: Specialty Products
businessLines.how: Sells branded and industrial lubricants and specialty products at premium prices to consumers, fleets and manufacturers; the highest-return segment on little capital.
businessLines.description: Lubricants (Mobil 1), basestocks, waxes, resins, and performance and asphalt products.

revenue.note: External sales and other operating revenue (5,502 + 12,269)

businessLines.revenueNote: External sales and other operating revenue (5,502 + 12,269)

businessLines.name: Low Carbon Solutions (inside Corporate and Financing)
businessLines.how: Pre-revenue or early stage; intends to earn fees and product sales from customers who want to bury or avoid emissions, subject to government policy support.
businessLines.description: Carbon capture and storage, hydrogen and ammonia, lower-emission fuels, Proxxima resin systems, carbon materials, low-carbon data centers and lithium. Not reported as a segment; costs sit in Corporate and Financing until it reaches material revenue.

brands.name: Pioneer Natural Resources (acquired May 3, 2024)
brands.share: U.S. net production 2.1 million oil-equivalent barrels per day in 2025, about 44% of the company's 4.7 million (share computed: 2.1 / 4.736; U.S. total, not Pioneer alone)

brands.note: Yellowtail started 2025; Uaru and Whiptail under development; Hammerhead funded 2025
